title: Installment Change Set
description: Installment-level membership actions for one proposal refinement, each naming the purchase it applies to by product_id and the installment by its closed canonical (collection_ref, installment_id) reference. A tuple cannot be an object key, so this is a list rather than a map. Unlike core/product-change-map.json, whose object keys make a contradiction structurally unrepresentable, uniqueness here is a requirement rather than a guarantee: entries MUST be unique by (product_id, installment_ref), and a seller receiving a repeated or contradictory pair rejects the request at task level with INVALID_REQUEST rather than applying the entries in an arbitrary order. Buyers SHOULD order entries by the JCS bytes of (product_id, installment_ref) so a rebuilt retry hashes to the same idempotency payload, and sellers MUST NOT make the result depend on order.

product_id.description: Product whose purchase in commercial_terms.purchases carries the installment.

installment_ref.description: Installment the action applies to. It MUST be one the named product's installments declare. The seller validates that product_id is purchased by the source proposal BEFORE resolving this reference, so an unauthorized caller never causes reference resolution; an unresolvable reference is then rejected at task level with REFERENCE_NOT_FOUND rather than returned as an unsatisfied change.

action.description: Required, because a drop that silently defaulted to include is the expensive failure. include requires the installment to be present in that purchase's installments in every returned draft; omit requires its absence. Swapping a slot is one omit plus one include in the same refinement.
